Human osteology: Introduction to osteology, bone function and classification, humerus, radius, ulna, femur, tibia, fibula, clavicle, scapula, ribs, sternum, vertebrae, pelvis, hand and foot bones, sesamoid bones, skull, mandible, joints. Introduction to organic chemistry: Chemical bonding in organic compounds, nature, physical properties and nomenclature of simple organic molecules, isomerism, chemical properties of alkanes and cycloalkanes, alkenes, alcohols, aldehydes and ketones, carboxylic acids and esters, amines and amides, carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids. module_catalog.name: People and their environment 112
module_catalog.content: This module comprises basic psychology and sociology concepts relevant to medicine, and to dentistry, in the case of BChD students. Basic psychiatric concepts are also taught.

module_catalog.name: Molecular and cell biology 111
module_catalog.content: Introduction to the molecular structure and function of the cell. Basic chemistry of the cell. Structure and composition of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Ultrastructure and function of cellular organelles, membranes and the cytoskeleton. General principles of energy, enzymes and cell metabolism. Selected processes, e.g. glycolysis, respiration and/or photosynthesis. Introduction to molecular genetics: DNA structure and replication, transcription, translation. Cell growth and cell division.

module_catalog.name: Medical terminology 180
module_catalog.content: The acquisition of a basic medical orientated vocabulary compiled from Latin and Greek stem forms combined with prefixes and suffixes derived from those languages. The manner in which the meanings of medical terms can be determined by analysing the terms into their recognisable meaningful constituent parts, is taught and exercised. The functional use of medical terms in context as practical outcome of terminological application is continually attended to.
module_catalog.prerequisites: No prerequisites.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week
module_catalog.service_modules: Faculty of Health Sciences Faculty of Natural and Agricultural Sciences Faculty of Veterinary Science

module_catalog.name: First course in physics 114
module_catalog.content: SI-units. Significant figures. Waves: intensity, superposition, interference, standing waves, resonance, beats, Doppler. Geometrical optics: Reflection, refraction, mirrors, thin lenses, instruments. Physical optics: Young-interference, coherence, diffraction, polarisation. Hydrostatics and dynamics: density, pressure, Archimedes’ principle, continuity, Bernoulli. Heat: temperature, specific heat, expansion, heat transfer. Vectors. Kinematics of a point: Relative, projectile, and circular motion. Dynamics: Newton’s laws, friction. Work: point masses, gasses (ideal gas law), gravitation, spring, power. Kinetic energy: Conservative forces, gravitation, spring. Conservation of energy. Conservation of momentum. Impulse and collisions. System of particles: Centre of mass, Newton’s laws. Rotation: torque, conservation of angular momentum, equilibrium, centre of gravity.
module_catalog.prerequisites: A candidate must have passed both Mathematics and Physical Sciences with at least 60% in the Grade 12 examination OR the candidate must have passed Foundational mathematics (WTW 137 and WTW 147) and Foundational physics (PHY 137 and PHY 147).
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 discussion class per week, 4 lectures per week, 1 practical per week
module_catalog.service_modules: Faculty of Engineering, Built Environment and Information Technology Faculty of Education

module_catalog.name: Physics for biology students 131
module_catalog.content: Note: PHY 131 is aimed at students who will not continue with physics. PHY 131 cannot be used as a substitute for PHY 114. Units, vectors, one dimensional kinematics, dynamics, work, equilibrium, sound, liquids, heat, thermodynamic processes, electric potential and capacitance, direct current and alternating current, optics, modern physics, radioactivity.

module_catalog.name: Basic emergency care 286

The student will be able to integrate the knowledge gained with the holistic approach to patients in order to be able to approach the treatment of patients preventatively and comprehensively.  The course will provide the dental student with a thorough basic knowledge of principles of infection in general microbiology and virology.

Where appropriate, case studies will be discussed in order to demonstrate the practical application of the gained physiological knowledge to the clinical management of a dental patient. module_catalog.name: Pharmacology 370
module_catalog.content: The purpose of the module is to prepare Dentistry students for rational prescribing of pharmacotherapy. Furthermore, it will also allow you to have informed interactions with your patients and other healthcare professionals regarding prescribing and pharmacotherapy. Learning opportunities include: Pharmacokinetics Pharmacodynamics Autonomic nervous system Central nervous system Antihistamines and anti-emetics Therapy of anaphylaxis, asthma and other lung conditions Antibacterial drugs Antifungal drugs Antiviral drugs Antimicrobial drugs in the treatment of oral conditions Cardiovascular system Pain and inflammation Anti-diabetic drugs Peptic ulcer disease Drugs for ear, nose and throat diseases Drugs for skin and eye diseases Rational prescribing and drug safety Toxicology
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules in the second year of study.

module_catalog.content: Diagnostic imaging 380/480 is a two-year module delivered during the 3rd and 4th years of the BChD programme. It deals with all aspects of radiographic imaging of the maxillofacial region appropriate to the Dentist. Diagnostic imaging 380 is delivered during BChD III as a promotion module. Physics Radiation safety and protection X ray film, intensifying screens and grids Projection geometry and image characteristics Film imaging and processing of film Digital radiography Intraoral examinations Intraoral radiographic anatomy Radiographic interpretation of dental caries Radiographic interpretation of periodontal disease Panoramic radiography Panoramic anatomy Skull radiography Cephalometric radiography Professionalism and empathy Quality assurance and infection control

module_catalog.name: Comprehensive patient management 370
module_catalog.content: Holistic evaluation of a patient, the clinical hypothetic-deductive reasoning processes, diagnosis, prognosis and treatment planning. Under the guidance of a tutor, and by utilising a special “practice patient” file, the students start treating a “practice patient” comprehensively. The student compiles a portfolio, on a continuous basis, on the clinical and administrative procedures concerning the "practice patient". The portfolio contains the student’s year mark, which is determined on a 50:50 basis, with the examination mark as the final pass mark. The examination mark is determined when the student presents the practice patient case to an audience and a panel of adjudicators. Application of business management principles during patient management. Preparing the student for a meaningful and successful career in an increasingly complex business and health care environment. Application of certain principles and skills in terms of: •   Psychology in the dentistry practice. •   Political parameters in dentistry. •   Sociology and dentistry. •   Ethics for the dentist. •   Career possibilities. •   Management of a practice. Additional to this, students should understand the economic, cultural, legal and regulatory environment to establish and optimise patient management.
module_catalog.prerequisites: BOK 280,(BOK 281 or (BOK 285,287)),BOK 283,GNK 286,GNK 288,GPS 280,IKT 200,SMO 211,SMO 281

module_catalog.name: Comprehensive patient management 480
module_catalog.content: The significance of the module is that trends in modern Dentistry require that the dentist must possess not only exceptional clinical skills, but also exceptional relational communication between the dentist/oral hygienist and the patient, judgment and business skills to ensure a viable dental practice. This module integrates various soft-skill approaches with the clinical sciences and strives to integrate different modules in the dental curriculum horizontally and vertically in terms of clinical reasoning in order to foster professional and ethical behaviour and exceptional judgment and reasoning skills. The purpose of the CPM module is to teach students how to manage their patients and practices to ensure a viable dental practice with minimal risk. CPM interrelates with all aspects of the dental curriculum. It draws on business and behavioural and clinical research and attempts to integrate knowledge on a vertical and a horizontal plane in the dental curriculum. The critical cross-field outcomes include the following: Identifying and solving problems by using critical and creative thinking. Working effectively with others as a member of a team. Organising and managing oneself and one’s activities responsibly and effectively. Collecting, analysing, organising and critically evaluating information. Communicating effectively using visual and/or language skills in the modes of oral and/or written persuasion. Using science and technology responsibly, effectively and critically, showing responsibility towards the environment and health of others. Contributing to the full personal development of each learner and the social and economic development of society at large by making it the underlying intention of any programme of learning to make an individual aware of the importance of: Reflecting on and exploring a variety of strategies to learn more effectively. Being culturally sensitive across a range of social contexts. Developing entrepreneurial opportunities. The module comprises three study units namely: Comprehensive Patient Care includes application of a holistic approach towards patient care and recordkeeping in a clinical setting, combined with a portfolio assessment. A case-based approach is followed in the classroom and case studies form the basis of the classroom assessment. Ethics and Jurisprudence includes an overview of HPCSA guidelines and regulations as well as the main laws that govern the profession. Knowledge is applied by means of case discussions and mini assignments. Dental Practice Management focuses on career options, leadership, strategic management, teamwork, human resource management, marketing, and general practice management.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules of year three.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 other contact session per week for 5 weeks, 1 lecture per week, 1 discussion class per week, 1 seminar, 1 practical per week

module_catalog.name: Orthodontics 480
module_catalog.content: Examination of an orthodontic patient. Treatment planning. Treatment timing in orthodontics. The mechanics of tooth movement. Skeletal maturity indicators. Space maintenance. Biology of orthodontic tooth movement. Methods of gaining space. Orthodontic appliances- general principles. Anchorage. Arch expansion. Preventive and interceptive orthodontics. Clinical features of Class I, II and III malocclusions. Management of space in orthodontics. Vertical dimension in orthodontics. Aesthetics in orthodontics.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules of year three.
module_catalog.contact_time: Once a week for 18 weeks, 1 lecture per week for 38 weeks, 1 practical per week for 37 weeks, One discussion class per week for 15 weeks

module_catalog.name: Orthodontics 580
module_catalog.content: Module content includes: Orthodontic appliances– General principles & introduction to forces Overview of space management. Myofunctional appliances. Management of Impacted teeth. Management of Pseudo Class III. Management of Class I, II and III malocclusions. Bio-mechanical principles in orthodontics. Orthopaedic appliances. Retention and relapse. Clinical and management of cross bites. Clinical and management of deep bites. Surgical orthodontics. Clinical and management of open bites. Occlusion and temporomandibular joint function. Periodontics and orthodontics. Cleft lip and cleft palate. Adult orthodontics. Fixed appliances. Relapse and retention. Orthodontics in general dental practice.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules of year four.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 per week for 18 weeks, 1 practical per week for 30 weeks, One per week for 12 weeks, 1 per week for 30 weeks

module_catalog.name: Periodontology 480
module_catalog.content: The module is a continuation from year three Periodontology. The module has two components, namely Periodontology and oral medicine component. The following topics are covered under as part of Periodontology: Periodontal manifestations of developmental and acquired conditions. The treatment of infective periodontal disease. Mucogingival procedures of which include: Root coverage procedures. Gingival augmentation (vestibuloplasty procedures). Gingivectomy and gingivoplasty procedures. Clinical crown lengthening procedures. The following topics are covered in Oral Medicine: Examination of the oral medicine patient. Dentistry-related drug interactions. Special investigations or the oral mucosa. Treatment of infections. The clinical component that runs over two year (fourth and fifth) of the module has been designed to allow the dental student to: Perform a comprehensive clinical examination of the periodontal and oral medicine patient, including the assessment of any mucogingival defects requiring periodontal plastic surgery or dental implant therapy. Effectively screen the patient for oral mucosal malignancy and precursor lesions. Use the information gained to differentiate clinically between the various forms of periodontal and oral mucosal disease to arrive at a (differential) diagnosis. Design and coordinate a treatment plan for the treatment and prevention of periodontitis. Coordinate the treatment of an oral medicine patient, either through pharmacological management, surgical excision of relevant lesions, or referral for specialist management. Perform clinical procedures associated with the treatment of early and moderate stages of periodontitis.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules of year three.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 discussion class per week, 1 per week for 20 weeks, 1 lecture per week for 39 weeks

module_catalog.name: Periodontology 570
module_catalog.content: The module is a continuation from year four Periodontology. The fifth year offers basic theoretical knowledge in Implantology and a continuation from fourth year of Oral Medicine. Implantology topics that are covered include: Dental implant hardware. Applied anatomy for dental implants. Principles of bone healing and dimensional alveolar ridge alterations after tooth extraction. Principles of osseointegration. Similarities and differences between dental implants and natural teeth. Case selection. Implant placement protocol. Peri-implant disease. Occlusion on dental implants. Oral Medicine topics include: Adjunctive diagnostic aids used in the evaluation of potentially malignant disease. Burning mouth syndrome. Evaluation of a patient with xerostomia. Treatment of immune-mediated conditions of the oral mucosa. Use of low-level laser therapy (biostimulation) in Oral Medicine. Drug-induced oral lesions. Systemic conditions and the oral cavity. The clinical component that runs over two year (fourth and fifth) of the module has been designed to allow the dental student to: Perform a comprehensive clinical examination of the periodontal and oral medicine patient, including the assessment of any muco-gingival defects requiring periodontal plastic surgery or dental implant therapy. Effectively screen the patient for oral mucosal malignancy and precursor lesions. Use the information gained to differentiate clinically between the various forms of periodontal and oral mucosal disease to arrive at a (differential) diagnosis. Design and coordinate a treatment plan for the treatment and prevention of periodontitis. Coordinate the treatment of an oral medicine patient, either through pharmacological management, surgical excision of relevant lesions, or referral for specialist management. Perform clinical procedures associated with the treatment of early and moderate stages of periodontitis. The student must understand the treatment possibilities associated with the advanced stages of periodontitis, including open flap debridement, respective treatment modalities, guided tissue regenerative procedures and dental implant treatment, and when and to whom such patients are referred for specialist diagnosis and treatment, should this be necessary. Maintain the periodontal health of a periodontal patient and be able to provide a supportive periodontal treatment plan suited to the individual patients’ needs. Design and coordinate a treatment plan for the treatment and prevention of peri-implant diseases.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules of year four.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 discussion class per week for 5 weeks, 1 practical per week, 1 lecture per week

module_catalog.name: Prosthodontics 470
module_catalog.content: Module consists of a removable and fixed prosthodontic preclinical component, which extends into the final year of study. Large emphasis is placed on the removable aspect of especially full upper and lower dentures and in the last quarter of the year, an introduction to fixed prosthodontics and clinical techniques. Learning opportunities include: Removable prosthodontics: The emergency session and diagnosis (includes medical history). Relevance of existing / old dentures and social determinants of disease. Diagnosis and treatment planning (Options and timing). Occlusion for complete dentures Tooth selection and arrangement. Anatomical determinants of the post dam. Neutral zone. Psychosocial impact of edentulism in Immediate dentures. Immediate dentures -Clinical and laboratory stages dentures. Dentures stomatitis and Tissue conditioners. Relines and rebases. Alternative Treatments for the Severely Resorbed Ridge in the Geriatric. Single dentures and combination syndrome. Troubling shooting in complete dentures. Pick up impressions and clasp additions. Consequences of partial tooth loss (RPD 1). Removable partial denture Classification. Removable partial denture Surveying. Removable partial denture Clasps. Removable partial denture Major connectors and tooth preparation. Removable partial denture tooth preparation part 2. Removable partial denture part 2. Design exercise tutorial. Design exercise tutorial part 2. Patient needs versus wants versus possibilities and patient adaptations. Fixed Prosthodontics (Preclinical): Introduction to fixed prosthodontics & principles of crown preparation. Index. Metal crown preparation. Zirconia crown preparation. Fabrication of a provisional crown. Lithium disilicate crown preparation.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules of year three.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 2 sessions per week, 2 clinical sessions per week, 5 Preclinical Sessions

module_catalog.name: Prosthodontics 570
module_catalog.content: Examination and evaluation of the denture patient, principles and taking of impressions, determination of vertical and horizontal jaw relations and facial bow recording. Aesthetics. Fitting and placing of the finished denture. Post treatment. Clinical aspects of manufacturing of complete and partial dentures, obturators and special apparatus. Pre-clinical crown and bridge techniques course. Examination and evaluation of patient's requiring crown and bridge treatment. Principles of tooth preparation and impression-making. Shade selection. Finishing and cementation of fixed restorations. Clinical aspects of manufacturing of single crowns and fixed prostheses. An introduction to lasers and implants.
module_catalog.prerequisites: TBW 470,ODO 470,MFP 470,PDL 470,DFA 470,OFC 470,PRD 470,GAP 470,TMZ 470
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 practicals per week, 1 discussion class per week, 1 lecture per week

module_catalog.name: Prosthodontics 580
module_catalog.content: Consists of a removable and fixed prosthodontic component. The removable component consists of lectures and clinical sessions where diagnostic tools are implemented, treatment planning and patient treatment proceeds under supervision. The fixed component consists of lectures and completion of the preclinical module which started in the latter part of the 4th year. After completion of the preclinical module, students submit their typodonts and a preclinical skills examination ensues. After successful completion, students are allowed to perform treatment on patients under supervision. To complete the module, students must fulfil minimum clinical requirements based on a number of essential procedures stipulated in the study guide and perform them independently. Learning opportunities include: Preclinical procedures: Anterior lithium disilicate bridges. Anterior zirconia veneered bridges. Single intra-coronal indirect restorations. Direct and indirect post and cores. Removable prosthodontics: Emergency 1-2 tooth partials & troubleshooting in partials. Special impression techniques, palatograms etc. Denture duplication. Alveolar bone resorption - complex biological aspects. Functions of saliva. Treatment planning. Effects of radiation. Cleft palates. Overdentures and a brief overview of implantology. Maxillofacial prosthodontics. RPD design exercises. Fixed Prosthodontics: The consultation – and ethical aspects. Introduction to fixed prosthodontics & principles of tooth preparation. Full metal crowns & ceramo-metal crowns: i. The anterior crown ii. The posterior crown. Provisional restorations: Materials and techniques. Introduction to Ceramics and CAD/CAM dentistry. Partial coverage restorations: i. The Posterior Gold Inlay ii. The Posterior CAD CAM inlay. CAD/CAM workflow. Treatment planning in fixed and removable Prosthodontics. Restoration of endodontically treated teeth. The direct post and core and indirect post and core. Impression materials and techniques in fixed prosthodontics. Soft tissue management in fixed prosthodontics. Cementation for provisional and definitive restorations. Minimally invasive rehabilitation. Dentine sensitivity. Critical appraisal of dental literature. Aesthetics and golden proportions. Practicing beyond your expertise – an ethical lecture.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules of year four.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 discussion class per week, 1 lecture per week, 2 practical per week for 30 weeks

module_catalog.name: Diagnostic imaging 470
module_catalog.content: Diagnostic imaging 370/470 is a two year course delivered during the 3rd and 4th years of the BChD programme.  It deals with all aspects of radiographic imaging of the maxillofacial region appropriate to the Dentist.  Diagnostic imaging 370 is delivered during BChD III as a promotion course.  Diagnostic imaging 470  is an examination course delivered during BChD IV.  The purpose of Diagnostic imaging 470 is: - To formalise teaching and examination of Diagnostic Imaging 370/470. - To certify students’ ability to apply knowledge obtained in Diagnostic Imaging 370 to clinical and practical situations of Diagnostic Imaging. - To certify that students act professionally during clinical situations of Diagnostic Imaging.
module_catalog.prerequisites: GNK 388,MDB 370,TGG 370,FSG 370,FAR 370,GPS 370,TBW 370,ODO 370,PDL 370,ORD 370,OFC 370,TK 370,RAD 370
module_catalog.contact_time: One discussion class per week for six weeks, 1 practical per week (28 week period), 1 lecture per week for 30 weeks

module_catalog.name: Diagnostic imaging 480
module_catalog.content: Diagnostic imaging 480 is an examination module delivered during BChD IV. The purpose of Diagnostic imaging 480 is to: formalise teaching and examination of Diagnostic Imaging 380/480; certify students’ ability to apply knowledge obtained in Diagnostic Imaging 380 to clinical and practical situations of Diagnostic Imaging; certify that students act professionally during clinical situations of Diagnostic Imaging. The module includes: Principles of radiographic interpretation Guidelines for prescribing dental radiography CBCT techniques. CBCT anatomy. CBCT interpretation. Radiology of the paranasal sinuses. Radiology of the TMJ. Specialised imaging techniques. Soft tissue calcifications. Legal aspects of dental radiography.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules of year three.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 lecture per week for 30 weeks, 1 practical per week (28 week period), One discussion class per week for six weeks

module_catalog.name: Diagnostic imaging 580
module_catalog.content: Diagnostic imaging 580 is an attendance course presented during the first semester of BChD V.  The purpose of the module is: To formalise teaching and formative assessment of final year students’ clinical and diagnostic skills in Diagnostic imaging. To develop students’ confidence in clinical aspects of Diagnostic imaging. To ensure radiographic service rendering in Diagnostic imaging by senior (5th year) students while 4th year students are in training.

module_catalog.name: Comprehensive patient management 570
module_catalog.content: Holistic evaluation of a patient, the clinical hypothetic-deductive reasoning processes, diagnosis, prognosis and treatment planning. Under the guidance of a tutor, and by utilising a special “practice patient” file, the students start treating a “practice patient” comprehensively. The student compiles a portfolio, on a continuous basis, on the clinical and administrative procedures concerning the "practice patient". The portfolio contains the student’s year mark, which is determined on a 50:50 basis with the examination mark as the final pass mark. The examination mark is determined when the student presents the practice patient case to an audience and a panel of adjudicators. Application of business management principles during patient management. Preparing the student for a meaningful and successful career in an increasingly complex business and health care environment. Application of certain principles and skills in terms of: •   Psychology in the dentistry practice. •   Political parameters in dentistry. •   Sociology and dentistry. •   Ethics for the dentist. •   Career possibilities. •   Managing a practice. Additional to this, students should understand the economic, cultural, legal and regulatory environment to establish and optimise patient management.
module_catalog.prerequisites: DFA 470,GAP 470,MFP 470,ODO 470,OFC 470,PDL 470,TBW 470,PTK 470,TMZ 470

module_catalog.name: Anaesthesiology 470
module_catalog.content: The module will empower the student with a wide general knowledge of the practice of anaesthesia and sedation as it relates to dental practice: Components and basic practice principles, physiological effects of general and regional anesthesia. Informed consent, risks and negligence. Pre-operative assessment (including special investigations and risk stratification, premedication) of patients for dental anaesthesia. Airway assessment, management. Monitoring of the anaesthetised / sedated patient. Equipment used in administration of anaesthesia. Post-operative recovery, monitoring, complications, discharge from recovery room. Pharmacology (pharmacodynamics and -kinetics, mechanism of action, side-effects, contra- indications, precautions in use) of induction agents, inhalational agents, analgesics, muscle relaxants and reversal agents, local anaesthetics, adjuncts and emergency drugs commonly used in dental practice Pharmacogenetic diseases related to anaesthesia practice. Pharmacology of fluid therapy and blood products Anaesthesia emergencies, Basic life support, CPR. Anaesthesia complications and management. Oxygen delivery, hypoxia. Anaesthesia for children. Anaesthesia for dental procedures, management of complications. The head injured patient. Conscious sedation.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules of year three.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 lecture per week, 1 discussion class per week
